One improvement · learn a related, larger task first
Training on MNLI first lifts RTE by 14 points
Why it can work
RTE is tiny: 2,490 training pairs, only 234 updates.
MNLI = Multi-Genre Natural Language Inference: 392,702 pairs from fiction, government, phone calls…
It asks almost the same question (entailment, neutral or contradiction?) with 158× more pairs.
The BERT authors also saw MNLI help RTE (footnote 14) but gave no numbers.
How much
+14.3
points of RTE dev accuracy
63.0 ± 2.7 → 77.3 ± 0.9, mean of 5 seeds; higher on all 5.
Cost: one 36-minute MNLI fine-tune for all 5 seeds.

Summary and evaluation
BERT’s results reproduce, with caveats on small tasks
What we reproduced
0.6
max gap to the paper on the same dev sets
MNLI-m −0.4 · SST-2 +0.3 · MRPC −0.6 with the paper’s lr search
6 of 7
tasks within 1.3 of an independent re-run
Hugging Face run_glue; RTE (−2.7) is the exception
209
fine-tuning runs on one RTX 5090 laptop GPU
7 of the paper’s 8 GLUE tasks · 8.7 GPU hours for the whole project
+14.3
RTE points from one change: MNLI first
63.0 ± 2.7 → 77.3 ± 0.9, mean of 5 seeds
Our recipe: BERT-Base, lr 2e-5, 3 epochs, batch 32, GLUE dev sets
Our evaluation
Strengths
+
Bidirectional pre-training (masked LM + NSP): beats GPT-1 on all 6 tasks we ran with the same recipe
+
Public checkpoints + a simple recipe reproduce the numbers
+
Fine-tuning is cheap: one MRPC run takes 18–28 s
Weaknesses
−
No variance reported: ±1–3 points by seed; lr picked on dev
−
Dev and test numbers mixed: RTE, STS-B and CoLA are test only
−
Optimizer details matter: without Adam bias correction, 4 of 6 BERT-Large RTE seeds collapse; with it, 0 of 6
4
/ 5
Reproducibility · our team’s rating
Claims hold; −1 for unreported variance and fragile small-task results
